requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the most likely hazards you may encounter while participating in water sports activities and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, and respond to these hazards. (b) Review prevention, symptoms, and first-aid treatment for the following injuries or illnesses that could occur while participating in water sports: blisters, cold-water shock and hypothermia, dehydration, heat-related illnesses, sunburn, sprains, strains, minor cuts and bruises, spinal injury, and concussions and head trauma. (c) Review the Scouting America Safety Afloat policy. Tell how it applies to water sports.

pamphlet_excerpts: Body Temperature Degrees: A body temperature of 105 degrees or greater is a life-threatening medicalcondition and requires immediate medical treatment by health-care.
Heatstroke Life-threatening: Heatstroke is a life-threatening condition; call for medical assistanceimmediately.
Waiting Medical Personnel: While waiting for medical personnel to arrive, work to lowerthe victim’s temperature.
Move Person Air-conditioned: Move the person to an air-conditioned or shadyarea.
step_by_step_procedure: Loosen Tight Clothing: Loosen tight clothing and further cool the victim by fanning and applying wet towels.
Possible Immerse Spray: If possible, immerse or spray the person with cold water.
Ifyou Ice Packs: Ifyou have ice packs, wrap them in a thin barrier (such as a thin towel) and place them under the armpits and against the neck and groin.
Personis Drink Small: If the personis able to drink, give small amounts of cool water.

Individual Buddy Craftshould: Every individual must have a buddy, and every craftshould have a buddy boat when on the water. 6.

pamphlet_excerpts: Driver Signal Alertthe: The driver may use this signal to alertthe skier that the boat is about to turn.
Skier Wants Driver: If the skier wants the driver to turn, theskier uses the same signal followed bypointing in the direction he or shewants the driver to go.
Once Skier Underway: Once a skier is underway, the noise from the boat makes hearing instructions difficult.
Skier Learn Directions: The skier must learn to give directions by using the hand signals shown here.
step_by_step_procedure: Observer Serves Eyes: The observer serves as the eyes and the ears for the driver and skier.
Skier Refers Water-skiers: Note that “skier” refers to both water-skiers and wakeboarders.
Observer Communicate Skier: The observer must communicate the skier’s signals to the boatdriver quickly and accurately.
Observer Mustwatch Skier: To do this, the observer mustwatch the skier closely, tell the boat driver if the skier falls, and keep the driver alert to other boat traffic.

pamphlet_excerpts: Putslightly Moreweight: To keep the boardfrom wobbling, putslightly moreweight on yourfront foot than onyour back foot asthe boat begins Alternate Method for Deepwater.
Youmay Prefer Start: Youmay prefer to start out with the wakeboard partially rotated uptoward the front foot.
Begin Wakeboard Out: Begin with the wakeboard out in front ofyou and parallel to the water’s surface, as before.
Yourknees Bent Hold: Keep yourknees bent and hold the rope handle with your arms straight.
step_by_step_procedure: Position Ready Shout: When you are in position and ready, shout out “Hit it!” to letthe driver know to accelerate.
Soon Boat Starts: As soon as the boat starts to pull, twist at the hips to turnthe front of the board up and toward the boat.
Yourknees Bent Transfer: Keeping yourknees bent, transfer more weight to your back foot as the boatpulls you up.
Alternate Starting Position: Alternate starting position to pull you out ofthe water.

pamphlet_excerpts: Wakeboards Angle Yourfeet: With wakeboards, the angle of yourfeet on the board can be adjusteddepending on your skill level.
Beginner Want Followthe: As a beginner, you’ll want to followthe steps below, fine-tuning theadjustments to find a stance thatfeels most comfortable to you.
Adjust Distancebetween: Step 1, Adjust the distancebetween the bindings to aboutshoulder-width apart, with yourback foot slightly more toward therear of the board for better.
Adjust Angle Theback: Step 2, Adjust the angle of theback foot so that it is straightacross the board or turned outslightly toward the back (at zeroto 9 degrees.
step_by_step_procedure: Adjust Angle Frontfoot: Step 3, Adjust the angle of the frontfoot so that it is slightly turned outtoward the front (9 to 27 degrees).
Board Size Youhit: Try the board on for size before youhit the water.
Foot Front: When riding a wakeboard, one foot is in front of the other.
Having Leftfoot Forward: Having the leftfoot forward is called “regular-footed,” and having the right footforward is called “goofy-footed,” but there is no right.
